name: judge0
summary: Candidate capability for sandboxed, multi-language execution of untrusted code.
why_it_matters: A future scenario may need isolated compilation and execution rather than the algorithm-library's current local fallback. This blueprint preserves the integration knowledge without claiming that the retired implementation is usable.
when_to_use: A concrete owning scenario must execute untrusted or generated code across multiple languages.
The owner requires a sandboxed execution boundary and cannot safely use a local process executor.

platform_support.notes: The retired Judge0 CE 1.13.1 implementation was API-healthy but could not execute a sandboxed program on the current Docker host. A future implementation must validate the actual execution path on every supported host; container health alone is insufficient.

prerequisites: A concrete owning scenario and a supported-use decision.
A dedicated isolate-compatible Linux execution environment that passes an end-to-end sandboxed submission check.
An explicit security, data-retention, backup, and platform-support design.
implementation_notes: Do not restore the retired Judge0 1.13.1 Docker Compose stack unchanged: its embedded isolate 1.8.1 failed at runtime with 'Cannot run proxy, clone failed: Operation not permitted' on the verified host.

A source-pinned current isolate build was also evaluated. Judge0 1.13.1 is based on Debian Buster, whose kernel headers cannot compile current isolate (missing io_uring syscall definitions); do not paper over that incompatibility with an unmaintained derivative.
Choose a currently supported execution backend and base image, then prove successful sandboxed execution before publishing a resource implementation.
Do not disable the sandbox merely to make execution succeed.
operational_notes: Health and language-list endpoints prove only API availability. Gate readiness on a real compile/run submission that returns an accepted result.
Treat submissions as retained execution data and define cleanup/backup policy before accepting real workload data.
The prior implementation accumulated 1,639 submissions but had no caller attribution, so operational telemetry must identify consumers before reintroduction.
risks: No active consumer currently justifies maintenance cost; algorithm-library intentionally uses its local executor.
Sandbox isolation depends on Docker, kernel namespaces, seccomp, cgroups, and image compatibility; these cannot be inferred from container health.
Executing untrusted code without a verified sandbox creates an unacceptable host-security risk.

references.value: Retired 2026-07-21 after verified Docker-host sandbox failure and no active consumer.
